escalations.question: T7 discovered that Edit preserves CRLF line terminators but normalises every EMBEDDED lone CR in the whole file, however far from the edit site -- measured 8 to 0 on backlog.md from an edit 220 lines away, and reproduced by the orchestrator on a purpose-built fixture at 2 to 0 from an edit six lines away. Criterion 1 permits only Edit on that file; criterion 20 requires the 8 lone CR preserved. The two are mutually unsatisfiable. T7 finished content with Edit then restored the 8 bytes with a byte-surgical binary write anchored on content.
escalations.answer: RATIFIED as done. The repair stands. Criterion 1's ban is on sed -i and Write by name AND by mechanism, both of which convert whole-file CRLF to LF; the binary restore does the opposite and was byte-verified by two independent parties -- the reviewer establishing that the first byte divergence between the pre-change copy and the current file is at byte 160126, which is line 477, the first edit site, so every byte before it including all eight lone CR is identical. Clause 1(c)'s letter is recorded as deviated-from with its reason. The generalised carve-out goes to the backlog rather than being amended into the criterion on a single instance.
